docs.title: Identity and guards
docs.text:
Two questions decide whether speculation is sound. Which request is this, so that running it early yields the same bytes as running it late? And under what condition may its result be kept? AgentIR answers the first with a content-addressed identity ladder and the second with a small guard algebra. Both live in agentir.core and are shared, unchanged, by the runtime, the serial reference interpreter, and the static compiler.

Identity is a function of program position and prompt structure. Physical attempts sit outside it. Open the diagram.

docs.title: The spine
docs.text:
A prompt is not a string. It is a canonical sequence of segments:

segment ::= Lit(atoms)                 constant atoms, known at trace time
          | Out(node)                  the sampled output of engine node `node`
          | Obs(tool_node, projection) one named projection of a tool result
spine   ::= [segment, ...]             adjacent Lits merged, empties dropped

Atoms are strings on the text wire and token-id tuples on the token wire; the IR treats them opaquely. The spine's content key hashes each Out as the producer's NodeId and each Obs as the pair (tool node id, projection id). That is why a continuation's key is computable before a single token of its producer exists.

docs.title: The identity ladder
docs.text:
DrawId names one logical random draw. It is (scope, occ, lane): scope digests the lexical call site together with the loop-structure path, occ counts dynamic executions within that scope, lane indexes the k siblings of an expand. The tracer reserves it at the DSL call, on the tracer thread, before it looks at any guard. Reserving at trace time is the load-bearing choice: it makes identity a function of program position alone, never of resolution timing.

Loops matter here. Each round of loop (and each tool-loop turn, and each call slot) pushes a path token, so an over-unrolled round consumes occurrences only inside its own scope. A draw made after the loop gets the same DrawId no matter how far ahead the tracer ran.

NodeId is a blake2b digest of the canonical descriptor: spine, model role, frozen sampling parameters, DrawId, and observation mode ("", "logprobs", or a stream projection identity). Everything the request is, nothing about how it runs. The hash is factored into named chunks (lit_chunk, out_chunk, node_identity_tail, finalize_node_id) so the static compiler can precompute the constant part and finalize later with the dynamic hole digests, byte for byte the same stream.

Seed is H(run_seed / invocation_id, NodeId). A node samples the same tokens whether it is issued speculatively or after its guard resolved. The problem_key you pass to run is a log label and enters no key; invocation_key scopes seeds, so benchmark arms that must sample the same tokens pass the same one.

Attempt is a physical engine request with a fresh id i{iid}-{node}-a{n}. Retries, preemptions, and engine restarts create new attempts of the same node. Attempts never enter NodeId or the seed, so "having tried a node early" can never change what it produces.

The only DrawId sharing in the system is across the mutually exclusive world instances of one hoist: one logical draw, several guards, at most one commit. Siblings share the draw but not the NodeId, because their spines differ, so the shared draw never licenses adopting one world's bytes into another.

docs.title: Sampling parameters are part of identity
docs.text: Every parameter is validated and canonicalized before hashing. The engine adapter maps or rejects each field; a key vLLM would silently drop must never enter identity. The accepted set is max_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, logit_bias, stop, stop_token_ids, repetition_penalty, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, logprob_topk, skip_special_tokens, include_stop_str_in_output, structured. Structured constraints are re-serialized deterministically so whitespace drift cannot split identity.

docs.title: Tool identity
docs.text: A TNode hashes tool name, canonical JSON arguments, DrawId, and effect class. It excludes the projection: how a program reads an observation is not a property of the execution. Projections have their own content identity (name plus a descriptor of the callable), so two projections of one body are two Obs segments over one T-node, and adding a projection never re-executes a body.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
A Decision is an unresolved selection event. choose creates one with pool keys and k; gate creates one with the two members @gate:true and @gate:false. Resolution is terminal and exactly once: either resolve(slots) with validated positions, or fail(cause). The two are distinct on purpose. A failed decision surfaces its cause to consumers; an empty resolution squashes silently.

Rankings are validated before they become resolutions: integers only, in range, no duplicates, at least k of them. An invalid ranking fails the decision, and the failure surfaces at its consumers exactly where the serial program would have raised.

A decision also carries its own entry guard: the world in which the decision itself exists. A decision inside a losing branch never exists, and its literals read as false rather than as its own failure.

docs.title: Guards: a conjunction of literals
docs.text:
A guard is a set of atoms At(d, r, s): "decision d's resolution has length greater than r, and its r-th slot is member s". A guard is one conjunction, one world. There is no disjunction and no merging of worlds a cleverer system might share; two instances a cleverer system would merge are simply two instances, mutually exclusive, at most one of which commits.

Evaluation is four-valued:

Value Meaning pending some literal's decision (or that decision's entry guard) is unresolved true every literal holds false some literal is contradicted, or two literals name different members for the same (d, r) failed(cause) a deciding computation raised, and nothing masks it

The conjunction rule is short-circuit evaluation lifted to speculation:

AND:  any false    → false
      else any pending → pending
      else any failed  → failed   (cause = the failed decision with the smallest creation ordinal)
      else true

False dominates failed because a false conjunct makes the world unreachable: in the source program the failing computation would never have run, so its exception must be unobservable. Pending precedes failed because a still-pending conjunct may yet turn false and erase the failure. When several conjuncts fail, the surfaced cause is chosen by stable decision order, never by which one finished first, so the observed exception cannot depend on a race.

Two derived quantities drive scheduling. guard_depth counts the distinct decisions whose literals are still pending on a guard; the window W bounds it. rank_sum adds the literal ranks; a rank-0 world is structurally more likely to commit than a rank-2 world, so it is funded first.

canon_guard drops literals already evaluated true, so a resolved-true prefix collapses out of a chain and a deep continuation's guard shrinks as decisions land. It never drops pending, false, or failed literals.

docs.title: Programs and handles
docs.text: An AgentIR program is a Python function that calls eight primitives. The primitives never return strings. They return handles: symbolic values that describe work and remember what it depends on. This page explains the three handles and the primitives that create and consume them. The rest of the pipeline exists to execute what these handles describe.

docs.title: Why handles instead of strings
docs.text:
If infer returned the generated text, the program would have to wait for it before doing anything else, and every decision would become a full stop. Returning a handle lets the tracer keep running ahead: it can build a prompt that refers to an output that does not exist yet, hash that prompt, and register the request. The scheduler fills in the bytes later.

Handles also carry provenance. When you concatenate a candidate into a judge prompt, the judge node records a data edge to the candidate node. That edge is what tells the scheduler when the judge can start, and what lets the engine's prefix cache reuse the candidate's KV blocks.

docs.title: The three handles
docs.text:
Handle Stands for Readable? Created by Seq An immutable token sequence: a canonical spine of literal segments and symbolic output segments. Only through an exit: text, out_text, force. lit, cat, fmt, infer, expand, obs Val[T] A control-plane future. Carries the node ids it awaited and the entry guard of the world it was created in. force(val), or as an input to another op. op, collect, out_text, text, logprobs_of, observe, ack Choice Rank r of decision d over a pool: "whichever member d ranks r-th". Never blocks. Only after binding: force, or continue it with infer/cat. choose, gate, expect, classify

All three raise TypeError on bool(). A handle has no truth value yet; the silent always-true reading of an object would be a bug waiting to happen, so it is refused at the coercion site.

docs.title: Seq: state semantics
docs.text:
infer(x) returns x's spine plus a new output segment. That is, a Seq is a state, not a delta:

draft = infer(prompt)                 # spine: [Lit(prompt), Out(draft_node)]
review = infer(cat(draft, lit(ask)))  # spine: [Lit(prompt), Out(draft_node), Lit(ask), Out(review_node)]
text(review)      # Val[str]: prompt + draft + ask + review
out_text(review)  # Val[str]: just the review

Two Seqs with the same spine are the same handle (key is a content hash of the spine). Adjacent literals are merged and empty ones dropped, so how you happened to build a prompt does not change its identity.

docs.title: Val: content untracked, world tracked
docs.text:
A Val wraps a concurrent.futures.Future, but it is more than a future. It records depends_nodes, the engine nodes whose output it transitively awaited, and entry_guard, the guard under which it was minted. Exits use the first to know what to wait for; force uses the second to refuse to publish a value from a world that lost.

An op runs its function on a worker pool as soon as its inputs resolve. With pure=True that may be on speculative data. With the default pure=False the op is an execution-delay barrier: it waits until its entry guard is true and every dependency it will read has committed, and it runs at most once. Declare pure=True only for deterministic functions with no external effects; it is a promise you make, not something Python checks.

docs.title: Choice: a placeholder with a decision behind it
docs.text:
best = choose(candidates, by=ranking, k=1)[0]   # Choice(d, rank 0)
top2 = choose(candidates, by=ranking, k=2)      # [Choice(d, 0), Choice(d, 1)]

A Choice holds a Decision and a mapping from member key to member handle. derive(fn) maps every member, which is how cat(best, tail) produces a new Choice over cat(A, tail), cat(B, tail), and so on. bound() returns the concrete member once the decision resolved, or None if this rank does not exist in that world (a false gate, or a failed decision's empty resolution).

docs.title: The eight primitives
docs.text:
Primitive Role What it registers lit(s) / cat(*xs) Build prompts Nothing: pure spine construction infer(x, **params) Continue once One engine node per possible world of x expand(x, k, **params) k continuations k nodes with identical prompts and distinct lanes of one draw text(x) / out_text(x) Observe A Val[str] exit; provenance stops here op(f, *args, pure=...) Compute on the control plane A pooled task; pure chooses replay-on-speculation or barrier choose(pool, by, k) Select by index A Decision and k Choice placeholders gate(x, cond) Keep or squash A two-slot decision with only a keep member loop(init, body, max_iters) Repeat with an entry predicate One gate decision per round, traced ahead of resolution

Helpers: collect gathers Vals in list order without occupying a worker per element; force is the blocking, publication-checked exit; fmt is cat with named holes; logprobs_of and top_logprobs_of read observation channels requested at generation time.

docs.title: Two effect classes
docs.text:
Everything on the control plane is one of two things:

  • Pure: replayable. May run on speculative inputs; its result and its exceptions are published only when its world commits, and the exits enforce that.
  • Unknown: the default for op, and for tools. Fenced until its entry guard is true and the dependencies it actually reads have committed. Runs at most once. Never retried.

An op whose result is a handle is not a routing mechanism. Continuing from a Val that holds a Seq makes the tracer wait for the value first. It is correct, merely slow. A program that wants speculation at a selection exposes that selection as a choose.

docs.title: What the rule "selection routes by index" buys
docs.text: Because choose returns positions into a pool that already exists, the set of possible continuations is finite and known at trace time. That is the precondition for the hoist in the tracer. It also means a ranking function, however elaborate, cannot inject new tokens into the dataflow: Seq has no public constructor from a string other than lit, and a Seq handed to a tool argument is rejected. The only way content leaves a Seq is an explicit exit, which is a provenance barrier by definition.

docs.title: The scheduler
docs.text:
The scheduler turns the guarded graph into engine requests. Its job is stated in one line in the source: legality in, cost out. Whether a node may run is decided by data readiness and guard state; when and in what order is a cost policy. This page follows a record through its life, then explains the funding order, cancellation, retries, and engine recovery.

Status and guard evolve independently. A record can be done long before it is committed. Open the diagram.

docs.title: One thread, two indexes
docs.text:
The scheduler runs entirely on the runtime's asyncio thread. The tracer posts registrations, demands, and decision callbacks to it with call_soon_threadsafe; engine streams are asyncio tasks on the same loop. There are no locks in the scheduler because there is no concurrency inside it.

It keeps every record ever registered in records (needed for dependency wiring, results, and diagnostics) and a separate _pending index of records that can still issue. An issue pass scans only the pending index, so a long-running benchmark with tens of thousands of finished nodes does not pay for them on every wake-up.

docs.title: Admission
docs.text:
An issue pass runs after every event: a registration, a demand, a decision resolving, an attempt ending. For each pending, data-ready record:

Guard Condition Issue as true slot free on its engine, or a speculative victim can be preempted committed, priority 0 pending depth ≤ W, spec_inflight < β, fewer than 5 failed speculative attempts, no observation barrier speculative, priority = depth false / failed never; the guard callback squashes it

Committed records are sorted by data-ready time, then registration time. Speculative records are sorted by the funding order of the design:

demanded first  →  shallower guard depth  →  lower rank sum  →  higher effective hint  →  older registration

Demanded means a tracer thread is waiting on this record through an exit; refusing it could deadlock the decision the scheduler itself is waiting for. The effective hint is the record's own static hint plus every resolved member hint on the decisions its guard names, read at dispatch time. Hints come from choose(hint=...) and may resolve long after a record registered; because a descendant's guard carries its ancestor's At literal, fresh evidence about a candidate re-prioritizes that candidate's whole speculative subtree without re-registration. Hints are advisory: never validated, never part of identity, never able to change a byte.

SpecConfig.depth1_unmetered=True lets depth-1 continuations bypass β. Their population is already bounded by the decision's pool, so metering them only starves a late-finishing candidate's children behind deeper speculation.

docs.title: Committed work preempts speculation
docs.text: If a committed record finds its engine full, _preempt_for cancels the worst in-flight speculative attempt on that engine: deepest guard, lowest hint, newest issue. The victim returns to pending with its NodeId and seed intact and reissues when a slot frees. Speculation never preempts committed work. With the flags off, speculation cancels nothing except a predicted loser (see optimizations).

docs.title: Attempts
docs.text:
_issue creates an Attempt with a fresh request id and a task running Runtime.execute_node, which streams from the engine adapter and aggregates deltas into result_atoms, exact result_text, logprobs, and token counts. The record's live partial stream is aliased for two advisory readers (prefix prefetch and bound-commit truncation) but is never a result.

How an attempt ends decides what happens to the record:

Outcome Record stream finished done; children lose this dependency and may become data-ready; committed if the guard is already true, else waits cancelled with cause preempt, spec-preempt, prune, engine-dead back to pending, reissue later cancelled with cause squash stays squashed cancelled with cause bound terminal done with tokens-so-far, finish_reason="bound" (committed algorithmic truncation) engine error, speculative spec_failures += 1, back to pending; a node that merely tried early is never poisoned engine error, committed retry up to 3 times, then failed with source semantics deterministic projection error, speculative deferred; surfaces only if the world commits EngineDeadError begin engine recovery

Failure cascades along data edges: a child whose producer can never materialize fails immediately with the producer's cause, exactly where the serial program would have raised, instead of waiting forever.

docs.title: Guard callbacks
docs.text:
When a record registers, the scheduler subscribes to the unresolved frontier of its guard: every decision whose resolution could change the guard's value now. Because a resolution can expose deeper frontier decisions (a literal whose entry guard just turned true), _reevaluate re-subscribes and re-reads until nothing new appears; only then is waiting safe. Re-evaluation does one of three things:

  • guard true: mark committed, resolve commit_fut, write a ledger row if already done;
  • guard false: squash, cancelling any running attempt, keeping any atoms on file unpublished;
  • guard failed: squash with the deciding computation's cause, so consumers re-raise it.

Consumers hold two futures per record, stable across attempts: done_fut (data exists) and commit_fut (data may be published). Pure ops and speculative descendants wait on the first; force and unknown-effect bodies wait on the second.

docs.title: Engine death
docs.text: A vLLM EngineDeadError is process-global. The scheduler trips one fuse per engine key: it advances the engine epoch, cancels every in-flight attempt of that engine with cause engine-dead, clears any partial results they produced, drains them, and calls the adapter's restart at most engine_restart_limit times (default 1). An attempt that finishes while its epoch is stale is fenced before it can publish. If the rebuild fails or the limit is exhausted, every pending record on that engine is poisoned with the cause, which then surfaces only in worlds that commit.

docs.title: The tool scheduler
docs.text: Tool bodies do not share the op executor. ToolScheduler keeps two admission queues in front of its own thread pool: committed work always drains first; speculable bodies under a pending guard are admitted only when speculation is enabled, the guard depth is within W, and a separate tool budget (β, capped by worker count) has room. A queued speculative body is promoted when its guard commits and discarded when it squashes; a body that already started cannot be stopped, which is exactly what the speculable declaration licenses. Unknown-effect bodies are never retried. Tools and the tool loop covers the contracts.

docs.title: Bookkeeping you can read
docs.text: Every record writes one ledger row when its disposition is known: committed, wasted (finished or aborted in a false world), or failed. Rows carry the six timestamps, token counts, the engine-reported cached-token count, speculative, depth_at_issue, and finish_reason. Control-plane ops, decisions, tool bodies, and tool-loop templates append to a separate event list. Timelines and diagnostics shows how to read them.

docs.title: Tools and the tool loop
docs.text:
A tool call is where an agent touches the outside world. Two things about it are new compared to a model request: its body may have effects that must not be repeated, and its result is an observation whose bytes the runtime cannot predict from the graph. AgentIR handles both with explicit contracts, and then speculates across tool calls the same way it speculates across selections: by declaring candidate observations and guarding the continuation built on each.

A call is dispatched as soon as its arguments close. The next turn is decoded against a guessed observation while the tool runs. Open the diagram.

docs.title: T-nodes and the effect contract
docs.text:
A tool execution is a T-node: tool name, canonical JSON arguments, DrawId, and an effect class. tool(fn, args, effect=...) registers one explicitly; the autonomous loop registers them from parsed model calls. The body receives one argument dictionary.

effect When the body runs What you promise "unknown" (default) after its guard is true and every handle it reads has committed; at most once; never retried nothing, this is the safe default "speculable" as soon as the tool scheduler admits it, possibly under a pending guard; retried up to 3 times per phase extra executions and retries are harmless, and the observation is stable enough to replay

Cancellation is exact at the admission boundary: an unstarted speculative body is removed without ever running. A body that has already started cannot be stopped, which is precisely what speculable licenses. Arguments may contain Val and Choice handles anywhere in the JSON tree; they resolve before hashing, and every handle found becomes part of the unknown-effect dependency fence. A Seq in an argument is rejected: content leaves a Seq only through an exit.

docs.title: Observations: raw result, projection, image
docs.text:
The raw return value of a body never enters a prompt. A projection alpha(raw) reduces it to an image: a string, or a JSON-compatible value rendered canonically. Images are what obs(t) splices into a spine (as a late-binding Obs segment), what observe(t) returns as a Val, and what the verification harness records and replays.

Projections are named and content-addressed by a descriptor of their callable, so two projections of one T-node are two Obs segments over one execution and adding a projection never re-runs the body. The image is encoded to atoms lazily, at the first prompt that needs it; on the remote wire that is a /tokenize request worth not paying for a losing branch.

Three primitives turn an observation into a decision: expect(t, guess) is a two-slot hit-or-miss decision that injects the guess bytes into the hit branch; classify(t, cases) routes an exact image through a closed mapping; ack(t) resolves when the body finished, for gating on completion alone.

docs.title: Observation policies
docs.text:
The autonomous loop wraps each tool in a ToolDef whose obs policy has four methods:

Method Role new_session() a fresh call-local instance (shallow copy by default) project(raw) the pure projection slots(state, call) the candidate images declared before the tool result exists select(image, slots) pick one declared slot index, reading the lazy real image if it needs to

The built-ins: Exact (the real image, with any guesses verified by byte equality), Ignore(text) (a constant, never reads the result), Project(alpha) (a reduced image), and Enum(cases, by) (a closed set of representatives plus an optional real-result hole). hole() marks the slot that is filled by the real observation. Selection is evaluated once per call in an advisory scope where model generation and unknown effects are forbidden, so a selector cannot smuggle a new observation into the graph.

A guess is a predictor: a literal string, a callable returning a Val, or a callable that traces ordinary DSL calls (a draft model, for instance). A plain ToolDef(fn) with no obs and no guess gets the default draft predictor, a 32-token same-role sample whose candidate count is calibrated online from observed hit rates and latencies. A predictor that has not finished when the real observation lands is abandoned, so a slow guess never extends the critical path.

docs.title: One round of the loop
docs.text:
infer(task, tools=..., max_turns=N) runs the loop in infer_tools. Per turn:

  1. Render the conversation with the engine's chat template and tool schemas, and register the assistant turn as an E-node with a stream projection frozen into its identity: the model family's vLLM parser, structural constraints, and reasoning-parser state.
  2. Pre-reserve the round template. Before any byte streams, the tracer creates max_calls deferred call slots plus an overflow sentinel, each with an existence gate and a publication gate, and reserves the next turn's draw. Slot identity therefore never depends on parser timing.
  3. Stream and parse. Each engine delta goes through a fresh vLLM parser instance. A cheap structural scanner watches the argument bytes; when they could form a complete JSON value, the strict decoder tries, and a closed call is published to a per-node journal.
  4. Dispatch. The published call binds its slot to a real T-node. Speculable bodies start now; unknown bodies wait for the turn and its guard to commit. For families whose calls close early, the tracer also registers the predict-taken next turn: assuming this call prefix is the whole inventory, it declares slots, spawns one guarded continuation per closed candidate, and starts the selector.
  5. Terminate. At end of turn the full parser re-parses the entire text and must reproduce exactly the streamed inventory. Prefix guesses that turned out shorter than the real call list are squashed; the exact one commits.
  6. Select. When the real image lands, select runs once. A hit keeps the guessed continuation; a miss keeps the hole continuation, which is data-ready now that the image exists. Multi-call rounds keep one representative vector across slots, never a Cartesian product, and fall back to a concrete barrier on any unsupported shape.

The tool loop requires the token wire so that boundary and special tokens stay in the spine. Stop strings are refused in tool loops because they would truncate text without preserving the parser's boundary tokens.

docs.title: Why retries and replays stay exact
docs.text:
Every published call is journaled per logical E-node. A retried engine attempt replays through the same journal: it must reproduce the already-published prefix event for event, and a divergence raises ProjectionDivergence instead of dispatching a call twice. Deterministic parser failures are ProjectionErrors, not engine errors: retrying the same seeded decode cannot repair malformed syntax, so the scheduler defers the error while the world is pending and surfaces it only if the world commits.

Model families are resolved from an explicit table (GPT-OSS, Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3.5+, Qwen3, Qwen2, DeepSeek-V3.1, Llama-3, Mistral). An unknown model is an error rather than a silent Hermes fallback, because the wrong parser would reinterpret ordinary text as a tool call.

docs.title: The tracer
docs.text: The tracer runs your program on its own thread and turns every DSL call into graph registrations without waiting for results. This page covers the registration steps, the hoist that creates speculative branches, how gate and loop lower to decisions, and the pacing rules that keep the graph finite.

docs.title: Five steps per call
docs.text:
Every infer or expand performs the same bookkeeping, all in microseconds:

  1. Reserve the draw from the context's DrawLedger, keyed by (loop path, call site). This happens first, before any guard is read.
  2. Freeze the descriptor. Validate and copy the sampling parameters, canonicalize the prompt spine, compute the NodeId and seed.
  3. Attach the ambient guard. The guard stack is thread-local: whatever literals the enclosing hoist or loop pushed, plus the entry guard carried by the input Seq.
  4. Register. Create a Record and post it to the scheduler thread with loop.call_soon_threadsafe. A NodeId collision inside one invocation is a hard error: the same descriptor registered twice means identity is broken.
  5. Return a Seq whose spine is the input spine plus Out(node).

Nothing here blocks. The tracer thread pauses only at explicit exits (force), at embedded values (cat of a Val), and at the pacing points described below.

docs.title: The hoist
docs.text:
infer over an unresolved Choice becomes one node per member, each with a data edge from its member and a guard literal from the decision. Open the diagram.

When infer receives a Choice whose decision is unresolved, it cannot know which member to continue, so it continues all of them:

infer(ChoiceRank(d, r))  ⟶  for each member s of the pool:
                               push At(d, r, s) onto the guard stack
                               register infer(s) under that guard
                           return Choice(d, {s: continuation_s}, r)

Three details make this correct rather than merely clever.

  • One draw, many worlds. The occurrence is reserved once for the source-level call and threaded through every member (and through nested choices, when a member is itself a Choice). The committed instance therefore has exactly the DrawId the serial program would assign.
  • The result is again a Choice over the same decision. Chains of continuations stay symbolic; cat distributes over a single Choice among its parts.
  • Already-resolved decisions short-circuit. If d resolved before the hoist, only the surviving member is continued, and its literal, already true, collapses out of the guard.

The fan-out is bounded fail-closed. One source-level call may hoist into at most 4096 world instances; a nested pool whose cross product exceeds that raises at trace time with a message pointing at the fix (pace the loop), instead of flooding the scheduler until every ranking times out.

docs.title: Gate
docs.text:
gate(x, cond) lowers to a decision with members @gate:true and @gate:false and returns a Choice mapping only the true slot to x. Continuing it registers a node guarded by At(d, 0, @gate:true). There is no false-case fallback: forcing a gated-out value raises Squashed. A Val condition arms the decision watchdog; a plain boolean resolves immediately.

The cascade algorithm uses this to make an escalation conditional without a barrier: infer(gate(strong_prompt, rejected)) registers the expensive request under the reject guard, so with speculation on it can decode while the review is still being written, and with speculation off it runs only if actually rejected.

docs.title: Loops
docs.text:
Each round is traced under the conjunction of every earlier round's continue gate. Open the diagram.

loop(init, body, max_iters, lookahead) expects body(state) -> (next_state, continue) where continue is a Val. The tracer unrolls predict-taken: round t is traced under

g_0     = the loop's own entry guard
g_{t+1} = g_t ∧ At(gate_t, 0, @gate:true)

The producer of round t's condition carries g_t, the guard under which round t was entered, never its own gate. The deadlock "the condition waits for a decision that waits for the condition" cannot be expressed, so no exemption analysis is needed.

Unrolling pauses when the tracer is more than lookahead unresolved gates ahead (default: the window W, or 0 when speculation is off). A false resolution squashes the whole over-unrolled tail at once; the waste is bounded by the lookahead and paid once. The return value is the state that entered the round whose condition said stop. A crash inside a speculatively traced round is deferred until the loop knows whether that round is real.

docs.title: Pacing hand-written loops
docs.text:
Beam search is written as a plain for over rounds: expand, score, choose, expand. Continuing an unresolved Choice hoists into one instance per member, so with every earlier selection unresolved the instances multiply across rounds, pool^rounds. pace_unrolling(selections, lookahead) is the tracer-side throttle: it blocks while more than lookahead of the loop's selections are unresolved, waiting oldest first. Under the serial reference it is a no-op, because there every selection resolves inline.

Where the pace sits inside the round body decides what gets harvested. Pacing before the expand means round t's children register only after round t−2 resolves. Pacing after the expand registers the children first, so a candidate that finishes its step early gets its own continuation issued the moment its text exists, while the round's straggler is still decoding. Beam search chooses the deep position only when the window can fund depth 2 and the fan-out fits under the hoist cap.

docs.title: Barriers you can see
docs.text:
Construct Effect on the tracer force(x) Blocks until x is data-complete and its guard is true cat(seq, some_val) Blocks until the Val resolves and its guard commits; the string becomes a literal infer(val_holding_a_seq) Blocks for the value, then continues it as ordinary work cat of two independent Choices Refused; the lowering builds no Cartesian product settle(choice) Blocks until the placeholder binds; returns the member handle, not content

Each is correct and merely slow. The design deletes the alternative, opaque routing speculation, on purpose: a strategy that wants speculation at its pick exposes the pick as a choose.

docs.title: Watchdogs and retirement
docs.text: A ranking that never returns would leave guards pending forever. Every decision created from a Val arms a host-side timer (SpecConfig.decision_timeout, default 600 s) that fails the decision with TimeoutError if it does not resolve. When the tracer function returns, the runtime resolves every still-dangling decision to the empty selection, which squashes over-unrolled speculation and aborts its requests, then drains every op and tool obligation so a committed effect is never lost to shutdown.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
A faster run is worthless if it computed something else. AgentIR's claim is stronger than "same answer": with speculation on, the committed computation is byte-for-byte the computation the serial program would have performed. This page explains the two gates that check that claim on a real engine, what each one can prove, and the diagnostics that explain a run when something looks wrong.

Gate A checks the lowering; gate B checks the scheduler. agentir check runs both. Open the diagram.

docs.title: Why two gates
docs.text: Turning speculation off still uses the guarded lowering: hoists, guards, the scheduler. If the tracer built the wrong graph, both arms would agree on the same bug. So the first gate compares against something that shares nothing with the lowering except the identity layer.

docs.title: Gate A: the serial reference interpreter
docs.text:
SerialContext duck-types the slice of the trace context that the DSL touches and sets serial = True, so every primitive routes to an eager implementation: infer executes the request and waits, choose reads the ranking and returns the member, gate returns the value or a dead marker, loop is a plain for. No guards, no scheduler, no hoist. It shares the spine algebra, the DrawLedger, descriptor hashing, and seed derivation verbatim, so its draws are comparable with the guarded run key for key.

The differential runs the guarded program with speculation off, snapshots every record that produced content, and replays those outputs into the serial interpreter wherever a NodeId coincides. That construction matters: engine batching is not bit-reproducible in general, and replay ensures that engine nondeterminism cannot masquerade as a lowering bug. Tool images are replayed too, keyed by (T-node, projection), so an effectful body never runs twice.

The comparison is:

  • the final value, or the fingerprint of the final exception;
  • the per-draw logical trace, (scope, occ, lane) → (NodeId, output digest), for every committed draw. A bare multiset of node ids would miss two draws swapped into each other's positions;
  • the tool trace by (T-node, projection): identity, status, and image digest;
  • no draw or tool present on only one side; and a quiesced guarded run.

docs.title: Gate B: the scheduler differential
docs.text:
Gate B captures the speculation-off arm (committed nodes, atoms, exact text, failure fingerprints, tool bodies and images) and runs a fresh speculation-on runtime over the same program with the same seed scope. The on arm receives tool bodies exclusively from the captured replay map: it has no fallback to the user's callable, so a differential can never repeat an unknown effect.

Every committed node in either arm must exist in the other with identical atoms, identical exact text, the same status and failure, and the same tool semantics; the answers must match. Physical evidence (which nodes were issued speculatively, which were wasted) is reported but not compared: attempt histories are allowed to differ, committed computation is not.

One permitted difference exists. Under the bound-commit algorithm (see optimizations), a provably losing candidate's decode may be truncated at a timing-dependent point. Both arms mark such records, and the comparison accepts one output being a prefix of the other for exactly those records.

docs.title: What the gates do not prove
docs.text:
Replay isolates the lowering and the scheduler from the engine. It does not prove that an engine build is bit-reproducible across batch compositions, and it does not prove that a speculable tool returns the same thing when called again. agentir check --slow-tool-audit addresses the second: it re-executes every completed speculable body serially and diffs the rendered image bytes of every projection. It repeats declared-safe effects on purpose, and it is off by default.

The engine-free test suite uses fake engines to pin down ordering, retries, identity, guard semantics, and protocol failures deterministically. Real-engine checks (agentir check, agentir refdiff, the verification scripts) are the evidence that a specific model, parser, and server configuration behaves.

docs.title: The ledger and timelines
docs.text:
Every engine record leaves a ledger row: t_reg, t_data_ready, t_issue, t_first, t_done, t_guard_resolved, token counts, cached_tokens, speculative, depth_at_issue, finish_reason, and a disposition. Ops, decisions, tool bodies, policy selections, and round templates go to an event list. render_timeline draws them as a Gantt chart: one lane per node, blue while speculative, green once committed, red when wasted, a dashed line per decision resolution, and a control-plane band for ops. Stacked panels share one time axis, so a spec-off and a spec-on run of the same problem line up.

Timelines and diagnostics explains how to read one and what a disappointing run usually looks like.

docs.title: The ablation ladder
docs.text:
agentir bench --spec ladder runs four arms of one workload:

Arm What runs What the step isolates A0 serial the reference interpreter the source program, one request at a time A1 spec-off guarded lowering, no speculation dataflow parallelism the graph exposes A2 spec-on guarded lowering with speculation branch speculation A3 oracle spec-off with every decision replayed from A1 at creation time the decision-latency-zero upper bound

The realization ratio (A1 − A2) / (A1 − A3) says how much of the recoverable decision wait speculation actually recovered. Decisions are keyed by content (kind and pool digest, plus occurrence within the loop path), not by creation ordinal, so over-unrolling does not shift the replay map.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: The supported public surface is agentir.__all__ in 1.3.0, re-exported from agentir.tracing.api (the DSL), agentir.execution (runtime), agentir.tracing.tools (tool definitions and policies), and agentir.diagnostics.viz. Everything is importable from the root: from agentir import infer, choose, make_runtime. The same names are also reachable through agentir.api; agentir.__version__ reports the version.

docs.title: Prompts and generation
docs.text: lit(s) → Seq A literal from a string, or a token-id tuple on the token wire. cat(*xs) → Seq | Choice Concatenate Seq, str, Val[str], and at most one unresolved Choice, which the result distributes over. A Val part blocks the tracer until it resolves and commits. fmt(template, **parts) → Seq | Choice cat with named holes: fmt("Q: {q}\nA: {a}", q=seq1, a=seq2). infer(x, *, model="main", logprobs=False, hint=0.0, **params) → Seq | Choice One continuation of x. Over an unresolved Choice, one guarded continuation per member (the hoist). Over a Val holding a handle, a barrier. params are the sampling parameters; hint is an advisory funding priority. With tools={name: ToolDef} it runs the autonomous tool loop and returns the final assistant turn; extra options max_turns=8, max_calls=8, timeout=600.0, system=None, max_tokens=512, temperature=0.0. Requires the token wire. With projection= it uses a prepared tool-stream projection (advanced, see calls). expand(x, k, *, model="main", logprobs=False, hint=0.0, **params) → list[Seq] k continuations of x: identical prompts, lanes 0..k-1 of one draw, distinct seeds.

docs.title: Reading values out
docs.text: text(x) → Val[str] / out_text(x) → Val[str] The full state, or only the generated tail. Accept Seq, Choice, or Val. Resolve as soon as the data exists, even speculatively; publication is enforced by force. logprobs_of(x) → Val[list[float]] / top_logprobs_of(x) → Val[list[dict]] Sampled-token logprobs (request with logprobs=True) or per-position top-k alternatives (request with logprob_topk=k). collect(vals) → Val[list] Gather Vals in list order without a worker per element. The first failure in list order is surfaced. force(x, timeout=None) → value The blocking exit. Waits for x's data and for its guard to be true. Raises Squashed for a rejected world and the deciding computation's own exception for a failed one.

docs.title: Control plane
docs.text: op(f, *args, pure=False, label="", after=None) → Val Run f on the worker pool once its inputs resolve. pure=True allows execution on speculative data (a promise of determinism and no side effects). The default waits for its entry guard and its dependencies to commit and runs at most once. after orders the body behind other Vals without consuming their values. choose(pool, by, k=1, hint=None, predict_losers=None, bound=None) → list[Choice] Pick k members by index. by is a ranking (positions, best first) as a Val or a static int or list. hint is a per-member list of floats or Vals for funding priority. predict_losers is an advisory loser predictor. bound enables bound commit. Duplicate pool members and invalid rankings are errors. gate(x, cond) → Choice Keep x when cond (a Val[bool] or a bool) is true. No false branch. loop(init, body, max_iters, lookahead=None) → state body(state) -> (next_state, continue_val). Unrolls predict-taken up to lookahead unresolved rounds (default: the window). Returns the state that entered the round whose condition was false. selection_bounds(pool, bounds, k=1) → contest Open a bound-commit contest; contest.attach(i, score_val) adds evidence; pass it to choose(..., bound=contest). prefetch_on_stream(source, build, *, model="judge", chunk_tokens=None) Advisory cache warming for a consumer whose prompt is build(text_so_far). Text wire, speculation and judge_prefetch enabled, else inert.

docs.title: Direct tools
docs.text: tool(fn, args=None, *, name="", effect="unknown", alpha=None, alpha_name="", after=None) → ToolHandle Register one tool execution. fn(args_dict). args may nest Val and Choice handles, never Seq. alpha is the declared projection. obs(t, alpha=None, *, name="", alpha_name="") → Seq The projected image as a late-binding prompt segment. observe(t, alpha=None, *, name="", alpha_name="") → Val The projected image as a control-plane value. ack(t) → Val[None] Completion, with the body's failure if any. expect(t, guess, *, alpha=None, name="", alpha_name="") → Choice A hit-or-miss decision: the guess bytes on exact equality, the real image otherwise. classify(t, cases, *, alpha=None, alpha_name="", name="") → Choice Route the exact image string through a closed mapping to already-traced branch values; an unlisted image is a ProjectionError. calls(y) → ProjectedCalls Prefix-stable call slots of a Seq generated with infer(prompt, projection=tool_projection(...)). Slot i's .name and .args are early Val exits; len waits for the terminal inventory. tool_projection lives in agentir.tracing.tools.

docs.title: Tool definitions and policies
docs.text: ToolDef(fn, effect="unknown", *, obs=..., guess=..., description=None, input_schema=None) One entry of the tools= registry. input_schema is the argument JSON Schema. With neither obs nor guess, the default is Exact() plus the draft predictor; obs=Exact() or guess=None disables the predictor. policy= is an accepted alias of obs=. Export Contract Policy base class: new_session, project, slots, select; exact image through one hole Exact() real image; guesses verified by byte equality Ignore(text="done") constant image, result never read Project(alpha) image is alpha(raw) Enum(cases, by=fn) closed representatives keyed by by(raw); a hole() case admits the real result hole() / open() the slot filled by the real observation (open shadows the builtin; import it deliberately)

docs.title: Runtime and diagnostics
docs.text:
Export Purpose make_runtime(...) local main engine, optional judge engine, subprocess judge, or attached judge server make_remote_runtime(...) certified remote vLLM runtime on the token wire Runtime(models, *, role_aliases=None, spec=None, run_seed=..., default_params=None, wire=None, wire_mode="text", event_granularity="auto", op_workers=32, tracer_workers=16) the general constructor over {role: ModelSpec} EngineSpec, ModelSpec, SpecConfig engine, role, and speculation configuration Squashed raised by force for a rejected world render_timeline(panels, out_path, *, title="") SVG timeline from TimelinePanels (import the panel class from agentir.diagnostics.viz)

Runtime methods: run(fn, *args, problem_key="p0", invocation_key=None, **kwargs), submit(...) (returns a future), warm(timeout=3600.0), chat_prefix(messages, *, role="main", tools=None, ...), ledger_for(problem_key), events_for(problem_key), snapshot(), close(), and the context-manager protocol.

docs.title: Not in __all__, still useful
docs.text:
agentir.api.settle(choice) waits for a placeholder and returns the bound member handle. agentir.api.pace_unrolling(selections, lookahead) throttles hand-written round loops. agentir.api.speculation_window() reports the effective window. agentir.compile.shape_trace and StaticGraph are the static compiler. agentir.diagnostics.reference.reference_differential and run_serial are the verification entry points. infer_tools, tool_projection, and TimelinePanel remain importable from the root for compatibility.

Source: __init__.py, tracing/api.py, tracing/tools.py, tracing/policy.py.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
agentir drives real benchmarks and checks on in-process vLLM engines. agentir COMMAND --help prints the full option list.

Command Purpose Model needed agentir list print tasks and algorithms no agentir warm build the engine, load weights, exit yes agentir bench run a dataset slice under an algorithm yes agentir refdiff verification gate A on one problem yes agentir check gates A and B on one problem yes

Every model-executing command fails fast with install instructions if vLLM is not importable.

docs.title: Engine options
docs.text: --model (required), --judge-model, --devices, --judge-devices, --judge-process, --max-model-len, --gpu-mem, --judge-gpu-mem, --max-inflight 32, --wire {text,tokens}.

docs.title: Speculation options
docs.text:
--spec {on,off,both,ladder,fastbase} (default on), --window 2, --spec-inflight 8, --depth1-unmetered, --judge-prefetch, --ev-gate, --spec-preempt, --prune-margin M. The optional lanes apply to spec-enabled arms only.

--spec Arms off, on one guarded arm both spec-off then spec-on, same problems, same seeds ladder serial reference, spec-off recording decisions, spec-on, oracle replay fastbase phase-serial beam baseline, spec-off, spec-on

docs.title: Algorithm options
docs.text: Option Default Used by --k 6 self_consistency, best_of_n, heavy (n), sal_beam (samples per step) --width, --branch, --rounds 2, 2, 3 beam shape; --rounds is sal_beam's iteration bound --iters 4 reflexion, mcts --step-tokens 160 beam step, MCTS rollout --early-steps, --late-step-tokens 3, unset varying step budget --step-stop STR unset step delimiter (escapes decoded, so '\n\n' works) --max-tokens 512 main budget; also the beam finish budget --judge-tokens 96 judge rationale budget --scorer {logprob,judge,prm} logprob beam scorer --prm-agg {min,last,mean,prod} min PRM aggregation --bound-commit off beam early round commit (needs prm, min, step-stop) --phase-serial off beam decode/grade barrier --prune-margin unset beam loser predictor (prm, min) --no-explain off skip self-consistency's explanation --chat off render prompts through the chat template --temperature, --top-p, --run-seed 0.8, 0.95, 20260708 sampling defaults and seed

docs.title: bench
docs.text: --task {gsm8k,math500,aime2024,amc2023} and --algo are required. --n 10, --offset 0, --concurrency 1, --out PATH (default runs/<task>-<algo>-<time>.jsonl), --dump-ledger DIR, --runtime-graph [DIR]. Datasets download on first use into ~/.cache/agentir.

docs.title: check and refdiff
docs.text:
check defaults to --algo beam_search --task gsm8k; refdiff to --algo best_of_n. Both take --offset. check --runtime-graph [PATH] renders the two arms on one time axis; check --slow-tool-audit re-executes completed speculable tools and diffs their images. Exit status 0 means every gate passed; 2 means a divergence or a failed audit.

Source: cli.py.

docs.text: Defaults as shipped in AgentIR 1.3.0. Algorithms and CLI flags may override generation defaults; check the entry point you actually call.

Argument Default Meaning model required HF model id for the main role engine_args None extra AsyncEngineArgs (max_model_len, gpu_memory_utilization, ...) devices None CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value for the main engine judge_model None model for the judge role; otherwise judge aliases main judge_engine_args, judge_devices None judge engine overrides; judge_devices alone gives the same model its own engine judge_process False run the judge as an OpenAI-compatible vLLM subprocess (text wire only) judge_server_attach None attach to an already running judge server instead of launching one max_inflight 32 requests per engine; also becomes max_num_seqs spec None a SpecConfig, defaults below run_seed 20260708 root of every derived seed default_params None overrides for the sampling defaults wire "text" "text" or "tokens" event_granularity "auto" "auto" or "delta" chat_template_kwargs None canonical template arguments for main judge_chat_template_kwargs None inherits the main value when omitted; {} resets

docs.text: Field Default Meaning enabled True branch speculation on or off window 2 W: maximum unresolved-guard depth eligible for issue max_spec_inflight 8 β: concurrent speculative engine requests (also the tool budget, capped by workers) depth1_unmetered False depth-1 continuations bypass β loop_lookahead None reserved; loop takes its own lookahead argument and defaults to window decision_timeout 600.0 seconds before an unresolved decision fails with TimeoutError; None disables op_drain_timeout 600.0 seconds run waits for committed effect obligations at retirement engine_restart_limit 1 rebuilds per physical engine after EngineDeadError judge_prefetch False prefix cache warming (spec-on only) prefetch_chunk_tokens 64 new producer tokens between warms prefetch_max_inflight 2 prefetch lane per engine static_plan None a compiled StaticPlan ev_gate False expected-value funding gate ev_gate_p_floor 0.05 cold-start probability floor for the gate spec_preempt False speculative slot preemption

docs.title: Sampling parameters
docs.text:
Defaults: max_tokens=512, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95 (the tool loop uses temperature=0.0). Accepted keys:

max_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, logit_bias,
stop, stop_token_ids, repetition_penalty, frequency_penalty,
presence_penalty, logprob_topk, skip_special_tokens,
include_stop_str_in_output, structured

Any other key is a ValueError at trace time. structured holds exactly one of json, regex, choice, grammar, json_object, structural_tag. Tool loops refuse stop strings. A token-drafting engine refuses min_p and logit_bias. There is no seed parameter.

docs.title: Scheduler constants
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning COMMITTED_RETRY_LIMIT 3 engine failures of a committed attempt before the node fails SPEC_ATTEMPT_LIMIT 5 failed speculative attempts before the node waits for commitment SPECULABLE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT 3 tool-body attempts per phase for speculable tools _HOIST_WORLD_CAP 4096 world instances one source-level call may hoist into SPEC_PREEMPT_MIN_REMAINING_FRAC 0.25 a victim keeps its slot once this close to done PREFETCH_PRIORITY 1,000,000 engine priority of warming requests

docs.title: Threads and pools
docs.text:
A Runtime owns one asyncio loop thread (agentir-loop), an op pool (32 workers), a tool pool (32), and a tracer pool (16). A tool that re-enters the runtime (a sub-agent) needs at least two tracer and two tool workers to avoid self-deadlock.

Source: execution/runtime.py, execution/engine.py, execution/scheduler.py.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Attempt One physical engine request for a node; retries and reissues create new attempts, identity is unchanged Barrier A point where the tracer waits for a concrete value: force, an embedded Val, continuing a Val Bound commit A committed early-stop rule: a candidate is truncated once k rivals' final scores strictly beat its monotone upper bound Choice A placeholder for rank r of a decision over a pool; continuing it hoists Commit A record's guard became true; its result may be published Control plane Python ops and decisions that coordinate engine and tool work Decision A choose (rank k members) or gate (keep or drop) event, resolved exactly once or failed Demanded A record a tracer thread is waiting on through an exit; funded first for liveness DrawId (scope, occurrence, lane): one logical random draw, reserved at trace time by program position E-node An engine node: one model request described by spine, role, parameters, DrawId, observation mode Effect class speculable (may run early and be retried) or unknown (fenced until commit, once) Epoch An engine generation counter; stale attempts are fenced across an engine restart Guard A conjunction of At(d, r, member) literals: the world in which a node survives Hoist Rewriting a continuation of an unresolved Choice into one guarded continuation per member Hole The observation slot filled by the real projected tool result Image The string or canonical JSON a projection exposes from a raw tool result Invocation One runtime.run, with its own context, draw ledger, and seed scope Lane Index of a sibling within one expand Ledger Per-node timing, token, and disposition rows NodeId Content-addressed identity of an E-node; the seed derives from it Observation policy project, slots, select: what a tool result becomes and which guesses may stand in for it Projection A named pure function of a raw tool result (alpha), or the parser contract of a streamed turn Rank sum Sum of literal ranks on a guard; a structural prior for funding order Record The scheduler's mutable state for an E-node: status, deps, attempts, results, futures Seq An opaque token-sequence handle over a spine; content leaves only through an exit Spine Canonical list of Lit, Out, Obs segments describing a prompt Squash Reject a world: abort its attempts, keep any output unpublished Static shape The program's parametric graph, traced over symbols without an engine T-node A tool execution: name, canonical arguments, DrawId, effect class Tier-1 The certified remote render / token-in-token-out / derender protocol Val A control-plane future carrying its dependencies and entry guard Wasted A record that finished or was aborted in a false world Weak control dependency A keep-or-cancel condition that supplies no input bytes Window (W) Maximum unresolved-guard depth eligible for speculative issue Wire Atom representation: strings (text) or token ids (tokens) World One combination of decision outcomes; every guarded instance lives in exactly one

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Find the boundary that failed: import, engine start, tracing, a decision, tool parsing, or the differential. Then reduce to the smallest program that reproduces it.

docs.title: Installation and engines
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix agentir does not import wrong environment python -m pip install -e . in the environment that runs the program "vLLM is not installed" base package only install the vllm extra, or use make_remote_runtime the engine starts again and again runtime created at import time move it under if __name__ == "__main__": out of memory context, concurrency, or two engines on one card lower max_model_len, gpu_memory_utilization, max_inflight; pin judge_devices "engine version X != pinned 0.24.0" version drift re-certify on the new build or set expected_version=None knowingly "AgentIR requires vLLM scheduling_policy='priority'" engine_args overrode it remove the override token-wire runtime rejects two engines tokenizer programs differ use the same model id for both roles, or the text wire

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
TypeError: Seq is a traced handle with no truth value. You branched on a handle. Use gate, choose, or loop, or force deliberately.

NotImplementedError: cat over two independent choices. Force one selection first or fold both into one decision.

RuntimeError: hoist over draw ... more than 4096 world instances. A hand-written round loop is unpaced. Call agentir.api.pace_unrolling(selections) once per round, or use loop.

The output contains the prompt. text reads the whole state; out_text reads the generated tail.

loop returned an older state than expected. A false condition returns the state that entered that round. Put the accept/reject logic around that contract.

GraphBreak under shape_trace. Only the compiler is affected; the program still runs under the live tracer. The message names the branch.

docs.title: Decisions and cancellation
docs.text:
Squashed from force. You published a rejected world: a false gate with no alternative, or a losing handle that escaped its branch.

RankingError. Return distinct in-range integer positions, at least k of them, best first. Not scores, not booleans.

TimeoutError: decision ... unresolved after 600s. A ranking or condition never resolved. Check that its op can complete and that nothing waits on a future that waits on it. Raise or disable SpecConfig.decision_timeout for genuinely slow judges.

A cancelled tool still ran. A body that started cannot be stopped; only unstarted speculative bodies are cancelled. Declare effect="unknown" for anything that must not run in a losing world.

docs.title: Tools and remote
docs.text: Symptom Check "requires a token wire" tool loops need wire="tokens" "no audited vLLM tool family for model" the model is outside the family table; pass an explicit ToolFamilyProfile to the projection, or choose a supported model the tool gets keyword arguments bodies receive one dict unexpected small model requests ToolDef(fn) enables the default draft predictor; pass obs=Exact() or guess=None ProjectionError from select selectors return a declared slot index or None; custom errors are errors, not misses ProjectionDivergence a retry or the terminal parser disagreed with published calls; do not swap parsers to silence it, find the mismatched template, parser, or model state leaks between calls override Policy.new_session to allocate nested mutable state certificate route returns 503 the server's parser pair is outside the audited set, or a plugin is loaded HTTP 412 / 428 from the server the server instance or certificate changed; the client re-handshakes once, then poisons remote calls only arrive at turn end expected: remote mode is terminal-only

docs.title: Correct but slower
docs.text: Look at a timeline before touching window. Common causes: no decision latency to hide, a barrier (force, embedded Val, PRM text dependency) in the middle of the round, a saturated engine, an expensive predictor, or remote render round trips. Change one knob at a time.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text: Include the minimal program, versions of AgentIR and vLLM, model and parser, wire, SpecConfig, the traceback, and whether the failure reproduces with speculation off. For check failures attach the printed report and the timeline. Redact credentials from remote configurations.
